pages.text: When the sun goes down, Flick the firefly wakes up. His little lantern blinks on.
The moth flutters to the porch light, then finds a leaf to rest on. Flick lights the way.
The crickets tune up: chirp, chirp, chirp, all along the fence.
The jumping spider in the fence post says goodnight with a wave of two tiny legs. Flick blinks back.
The ladybugs are already asleep under a leaf, a little row of red buttons.
The beetle trundles home along the path. Flick lights the way.
The bees are all inside the hive, humming one low, sleepy hum.
The glow-worms in the bank turn on their tiny lights, one by one.
The katydid sings her last song and goes quiet in the hedge.
The moon comes up. Now the whole garden has a lantern.
Flick's friends blink back at him from the trees: on, off, on, off.
Flick settles on a blade of grass, his lantern fading soft and slow. Goodnight, Flick.
